Updated assessment using the Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS) as context:

- Policy stance remains highly accommodative (ELB, continued Treasury/agency MBS/CMBS purchases, active repo and ON RRP), consistent with the FOMC’s aim to support the flow of credit and ease financial conditions.
- SLOOS (mid-2020) indicates broad-based tightening of lending standards and terms:
  - C&I loans: significant net shares of banks tightened standards for firms of all sizes; weaker demand after initial credit-line draws; wider spreads, stricter covenants/collateral.
  - CRE: notable tightening across property types; weaker demand.
  - Households: tighter standards for credit cards, auto, and other consumer loans; weaker demand in consumer credit.
  - Residential mortgages: standards tightened, but demand was comparatively stronger (refi/purchase) amid low rates; nonetheless, banks expected further tightening and worsening loan performance.
- Implications: Despite easier market functioning from Fed actions, the bank lending channel is restrictive, likely moderating monetary transmission to the real economy and keeping risks skewed to the downside.

Adjusted overall tone: more negative than the FSR-based assessment due to credit supply tightening signaled by SLOOS.
